title: The toolbox
description: Borrow ready-made tools from Python's math module to measure the round tower.

tasks.title: Borrow tools that are already made
tasks.body: import math loads Python's math module, and math.sqrt(16) uses one of its tools: the module's name, a dot, then the tool. from math import sqrt brings in just that tool, so you can write sqrt(16).
tasks.detail: import math as m gives the module a shorter name. Once imported, a module stays loaded for the rest of the program. On this page only some modules can be imported: math, random, datetime, json, csv and re. Asking for any other, such as os, stops with a ModuleNotFoundError that says it is not available here.

tasks.code:
# Three ways to reach a tool
import math
from math import floor
import math as m

print(math.sqrt(49))
print(floor(7.9))
print(m.pi > 3)
tasks.note: math.sqrt() names the module each time. floor came in on its own, so it needs no math. in front. m is just another name for the same module.

tasks.question: What does print(sqrt(49)) do in a program that only has import math?
tasks.why: import math brings in the module, not each of its tools by itself: the tool is math.sqrt. from math import sqrt would make sqrt work on its own.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: try print(sqrt(49)) with only import math. Then add import os and read the message.

Ask for the radius of a round tower, as a whole number. Print three lines: the distance around it, which is 2 times pi times the radius, rounded to 1 decimal place; the area inside it, pi times the radius times the radius, rounded to 1 decimal place; and how many steps of length 1 it takes to walk all the way round, rounded up to a whole step. Use pi and ceil() from the math module.
tasks.starter: # Import what you need, then measure the tower
hints: The math module has pi, to many more decimal places than 3.14, and a tool that rounds a number up.
round(x, 1) keeps one decimal place. The steps are the distance around rounded up, so even a little extra is one more step.
With other names, for a square pen: import math, then edge = 4 * side, and math.ceil(edge / 3) is how many fence panels of length 3 it needs.

error_hints.text: math is a name only after import math at the top of the program. A tool brought in with from math import ... is used without math. in front.
Turn the radius reply into a number with int(...) before working with it.
With a radius of 1: 6.3 around, 3.1 inside, and 7 steps, because 6.28... rounds up to 7.
With a radius of 10 the area is 314.2. If you got 314.0, pi was 3.14: use math.pi.
A radius of 0 gives 0.0, 0.0 and 0 steps.
Check another radius: every answer comes from the reply.
Check a radius whose distance around rounds to a whole number of tenths.

similar_example.code:
import math
side = 2.5
edge = 4 * side
print(edge)
print(math.ceil(edge / 3))
print(round(math.pi, 3))
similar_example.note: A square pen instead of a round tower: the math module's ceil() rounds the panels up. Your tower needs pi as well.

other_ways.code:
from math import pi, ceil
radius = int(input("Radius? "))
around = 2 * pi * radius
print(round(around, 1))
print(round(pi * radius ** 2, 1))
print(ceil(around))
other_ways.note: from math import brings in pi and ceil by name, so they need no math. in front. ** 2 squares the radius.

other_ways.code:
import math as m
radius = int(input("Radius? "))
print(round(m.tau * radius, 1))
print(round(m.pi * m.pow(radius, 2), 1))
print(m.ceil(m.tau * radius))
other_ways.note: tau is 2 times pi, and the math module has it too. as m is a shorter name for the module.
